learn.hook: Our country has had many beautiful names. The very first line of our Constitution uses two of them!
points: Article 1 of the Constitution of India says: 'India, that is Bharat, shall be a Union of States.' So both India and Bharat are official names.
In the Rigveda, one of the oldest texts, the Bharatas are an important clan (group of people). The Rigveda also speaks of the land of seven rivers, 'Sapta Sindhu'.
The Vishnu Purana describes Bharatam as the land north of the ocean and south of the snowy mountains, where the descendants of Bharata live.
Another old name is Jambudvipa, 'the island of the jambu (jamun) tree'. Emperor Ashoka used the word Jambudvipa in his inscriptions.
An inscription of King Kharavela at Hathigumpha in Odisha mentions 'Bharadhavasa', an early form of Bharatavarsha.

example.q: The Vishnu Purana says Bharatam lies north of the ocean and south of the snowy mountains. Which features are these?
steps: South of India lie the seas: the Arabian Sea, the Indian Ocean and the Bay of Bengal.
North of India stand the snowy Himalayas.
So the text describes the land between the seas and the Himalayas.
example.answer: The ocean to the south and the Himalayas to the north.

learn.reallife: The word Bharat is printed alongside India on our coins and passports, and we sing 'Bharat' in many patriotic songs.

games.title: Ancient names
items: The Constitution says 'India, that is Bharat'.
These words are in Article 1 of the Constitution.
Jambudvipa is named after the mango tree.
Ashoka used the name Jambudvipa in his inscriptions.
The Vishnu Purana places Bharatam south of the snowy mountains.
It describes the land between the ocean and the snowy mountains.
Bharat is a name that appeared only in the twentieth century.
Forms of the name appear in texts and inscriptions thousands of years old.

quiz.q: What does Article 1 of the Constitution of India say?
options: India shall have only one language
Bharat is a group of islands
India, that is Bharat, shall be a Union of States
India shall be called Hindustan only
quiz.explain: Article 1 gives both names, India and Bharat, and says the country is a Union of States.
steps: Article 1 is the first article of the Constitution.
It says: 'India, that is Bharat, shall be a Union of States.'
So it gives both names. Answer: India, that is Bharat, shall be a Union of States
quiz.mistake: Does not know that both names are in the Constitution

quiz.q: What does the name Jambudvipa mean?
quiz.explain: Jambu is the jamun tree and dvipa means island or large landmass.
steps: Jambu = the jamun tree; dvipa = island.
So Jambudvipa = 'island of the jambu (jamun) tree'.
Answer: Island of the jambu (jamun) tree
quiz.mistake: Guesses a meaning not linked to the word

quiz.q: Which emperor used the word Jambudvipa in his inscriptions?
quiz.explain: Ashoka's inscriptions mention Jambudvipa as the land he ruled.
steps: Jambudvipa is an old name for the land.
Emperor Ashoka used it in his inscriptions.
Answer: Ashoka
quiz.mistake: Picks a well-known ruler from a different period

quiz.q: In the Rigveda, who were the Bharatas?
quiz.explain: The Bharatas appear in the Rigveda as a prominent clan.
steps: The Rigveda is one of the oldest texts.
In it, the Bharatas are an important clan (group of people).
Answer: An important clan (group of people)
quiz.mistake: Thinks 'Bharata' always refers to a place

quiz.q: Which text describes Bharatam as the land north of the ocean and south of the snowy mountains?
quiz.explain: This description of Bharatam comes from the Vishnu Purana.
steps: Bharatam: north of the ocean, south of the snowy mountains.
This description comes from the Vishnu Purana.
Answer: Vishnu Purana
quiz.mistake: Does not connect the description with the Puranas

quiz.explain: Sapta means seven and sindhu here means river.
steps: Sapta = seven; sindhu here = river.
The Rigveda speaks of the land of seven rivers.
Answer: Land of seven rivers
quiz.mistake: Mixes up 'sindhu' with ocean or mountain

quiz.q: King Kharavela's inscription at Hathigumpha is in which present-day state?
quiz.explain: The Hathigumpha inscription is in the Udayagiri caves near Bhubaneswar, Odisha.
steps: King Kharavela's inscription is at Hathigumpha.
Hathigumpha is in Odisha.
It mentions 'Bharadhavasa'. Answer: Odisha

quiz.q: Which two names of our country are both official today?
steps: Article 1 says 'India, that is Bharat'.
So both India and Bharat are official names.
Jambudvipa and Hind are old names, not official ones. Answer: India and Bharat
quiz.mistake: Thinks older names are still official

teach.ask: Gappu asks, 'Is our country called India or Bharat? Which one is right?'
teach.praise: So both are right! The Constitution says 'India, that is Bharat', and ancient texts used names like Bharata and Jambudvipa.
teach.nudge: What does our Constitution say about the two names? And can you tell me an old name from ancient texts?

revise.summary: Our country has old Indian names found in texts and inscriptions. The Constitution says 'India, that is Bharat', the Rigveda speaks of the Bharatas, and Jambudvipa appears in Ashoka's inscriptions.

learn.hook: How did a river give its name to a whole country? Let's follow the Sindhu!
points: The Sindhu river (called the Indus in English) flows in the north-west of the subcontinent.
The ancient Persians said 'h' where Sanskrit has 's', so Sindhu became 'Hindu'. Here it was simply a name for the land and people of the Sindhu river region.
The Greeks dropped the 'h' sound, and 'Hindu' became 'Indos' or 'Indoi'. From this came the word 'India'.
Later, the Arabs called the land 'Al-Hind' and Persian writers called it 'Hindustan'.
The Chinese pilgrim Xuanzang, who travelled to India in the 7th century CE, called it 'Yindu'.

example.q: How did the word 'India' come from the name of a river?
steps: The river was called Sindhu.
Persians said 'Hindu' for Sindhu.
Greeks dropped the 'h' and said 'Indos', which later became 'India'.

learn.reallife: The Indian Ocean, Indian cricket team and 'Hindustani' music all carry names that trace back to the Sindhu river.

games.title: From Sindhu to India
games.prompt: How the name changed, in order

quiz.q: The name 'India' comes from the name of which river?
quiz.explain: Sindhu became Hindu in Persian and Indos in Greek, which gave the name India.
steps: The chain: Sindhu → Hindu (Persian) → Indos (Greek) → India.
It starts with the Sindhu, called the Indus in English.
Answer: Sindhu (Indus)
quiz.mistake: Picks the most famous river instead of the Sindhu

quiz.explain: In Persian, the 's' sound changed to 'h', so Sindhu became Hindu.
steps: The Persians said 'h' where Sanskrit has 's'.
So Sindhu became Hindu.
Answer: Hindu
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the Persian and Greek forms

quiz.q: Which people dropped the 'h' sound and said 'Indos'?
quiz.explain: The Greeks dropped the 'h', so Hindu became Indos or Indoi.
steps: Persian 'Hindu' lost its 'h' sound in Greek.
The Greeks said 'Indos' or 'Indoi'.
Answer: The Greeks
quiz.mistake: Mixes up who changed which sound

quiz.q: What name did the Arabs use for India?
quiz.explain: Arab writers called the land Al-Hind.
steps: Later, Arab writers named the land.
They called it Al-Hind.
Answer: Al-Hind
quiz.mistake: Mixes up names used by different peoples

quiz.q: What did the Chinese pilgrim Xuanzang call India?
quiz.explain: Xuanzang, who came in the 7th century CE, used the name Yindu.
steps: Xuanzang was a Chinese pilgrim.
He called India 'Yindu'.
Answer: Yindu
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the Chinese name with Persian or Arabic names

quiz.q: Which name was used by Persian writers for the land, and is still heard in songs today?
quiz.explain: 'Hindustan' comes from Persian and means the land of the Hindu (Sindhu) river region.
steps: Persian writers called the land 'Hindustan'.
Al-Hind is Arab; Indoi is Greek.
Answer: Hindustan
quiz.mistake: Thinks Hindustan is a Sanskrit name from the Vedas

quiz.q: In which century CE did Xuanzang travel to India?
quiz.explain: Xuanzang travelled across India in the 7th century CE.
steps: Xuanzang travelled to India in the 7th century CE.
Answer: 7th century

quiz.q: Why did many foreign names for India come from the Sindhu river?
options: The Sindhu is the only river in India
The Sindhu flows through every state
The Sindhu is in the far south
Travellers from the north-west first met the land of the Sindhu
quiz.explain: People coming from Persia and beyond reached the Sindhu region first, so they named the land after it.
steps: The Sindhu flows in the north-west.
Travellers from Persia and beyond reached this region first.
So they named the land after the river.
Answer: Travellers from the north-west first met the land of the Sindhu
quiz.mistake: Does not connect the river's location with the name

revise.summary: Many names for our land came from the Sindhu river. The Persians said Hindu, the Greeks said Indos, which gave 'India'; Arabs said Al-Hind, Persian writers Hindustan, and Xuanzang Yindu.

Why foreign names came from the Sindhu region
traps: Don't say the Greeks changed 's' to 'h'; the Persians did, and the Greeks dropped the 'h'
'Hindu' here was a name for the land and people of the Sindhu region
